title: Professional Ethics
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 1: Security and Risk Management: Professional Ethics.

items: CISSP holders must comply with the ISC2 Code of Professional Ethics
Applies to all ISC2 members globally — no exceptions
Agreement and strict adherence is a condition of gaining AND maintaining CISSP
Code consists of a Preamble and four Canons
Violation can result in certification revocation

blocks.text: The ISC2 Code of Professional Ethics Preamble states: "The safety and welfare of society and the common good, duty to our principals, and to each other, requires that we adhere, and be seen to adhere, to the highest ethical standards of behavior. Therefore, strict adherence to this Code is a condition of certification." All ISC2 members, including CISSP candidates, must agree to this code before attempting the exam. Ethical violations are taken seriously and can result in revocation of certification through the ISC2 Ethics Board review process. ⚠️ Exam Trap: The exam will likely ask at least one ethics question. Remember that the Canons are applied in order of priority — if a scenario presents a conflict between Canons, the higher-numbered Canon yields to the lower-numbered one (Canon 1 > Canon 2 > Canon 3 > Canon 4).

items: Canon 1: Protect society, the common good, necessary public trust and confidence, and the infrastructure
Canon 2: Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly, and legally
Canon 3: Provide diligent and competent service to principals
Canon 4: Advance and protect the profession

blocks.text: Memorize the exact order — the exam tests this directly. Canon 1 is the highest priority. Society and the common good ALWAYS come first. If your employer asks you to do something that harms the public, Canon 1 overrides Canon 3 (service to principals/employers). Canon 2 governs personal conduct. You must act with integrity even when no one is watching. Canon 3 — "Principals" refers to employers, clients, or those you serve professionally. You owe them diligent and competent service, but NOT at the expense of society (Canon 1) or honesty (Canon 2). Canon 4 — Contributing to the growth and reputation of the security profession. Mentoring, publishing research, and participating in professional organizations. ⚠️ Exam Trap: A common scenario: Your employer asks you to cover up a data breach. Canon 1 (protect society) and Canon 2 (act honestly/legally) override Canon 3 (serve your employer). The correct answer is to report the breach. Mnemonic: "Society → Honor → Service → Profession" (SHSP — "Ships") From Shon Harris: "Before you take this exam, be sure you understand and agree with the codes of ethics. In addition to these codes, all information security professionals should also support their organization's code of ethics."

items: Ethics are foundational to a successful security program
Ethical behavior = do nothing harmful to anyone else
Ethics vary due to culture, education, beliefs
Consistent ethics require codification in policies
Must be driven by management, top-down

blocks.text: Organizations must establish their own code of ethics in addition to the ISC2 code. The success of any security program requires ethical support from every level of the organization, driven by management and instilled through proper support, direction, and enforcement. From Shon Harris: "Certain structures can be put into place that provide a breeding ground for unethical behavior." Organizations must actively design their policies and incentive structures to promote ethical behavior. The best way to promote consistent ethical behavior is through corporate policies — rules that prescribe, promote, and instill ethical behavior. Policies must be legal, and adherence must start with senior management.
